flow.costPlain: Money set aside for loans expected to go bad — the closest thing a bank has to a cost of goods sold.

opex.name: Compensation and benefits
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the bank's roughly 212,000 employees — well over half of all running costs.

opex.name: Information processing and communications
opex.note: Technology, data processing and communications — the plumbing of a digital bank.

opex.name: Occupancy and equipment
opex.note: Branches, offices, ATMs and the equipment in them.

opex.name: Product delivery and transaction related
opex.note: The cost of moving money: processing payments, producing cards and handling transactions.

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Advertising and promoting the bank's products.

opex.name: Other general operating
opex.note: Everything else — this quarter it includes the $1.2B regulatory settlement charge.

follow100Note: People are the bank's biggest cost: $36.61 of every $100 goes to pay and benefits. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Banks don't report gross profit; this chart follows Bank of America's own structure — revenue, less the cost of expected loan losses, less running costs. Noninterest income and expense components are from its Q3 2026 quarterly financial supplement (Exhibit 99.3).
oneTimers: A $1.2B regulatory settlement charge sits inside 'Other general operating' expenses. It is not tax-deductible and cost $0.17 of EPS — excluding it, net income was $8.1B, EPS $1.08, and the efficiency ratio was 62% instead of the reported 66%.
Preferred stock dividends of $392M sit between net income ($6,933M) and the $6,541M attributable to common shareholders.
pngFooterNote: Component lines are from its Q3 2026 financial supplement.

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: The spread between what the bank earns on loans and securities and what it pays depositors and lenders — up 8% on bigger loan and deposit balances and repricing of older fixed-rate assets. The net interest yield was 2.16%.

segments.name: Noninterest income
segments.note: Fees and trading: wealth and brokerage fees of $5,761M, market making of $2,360M, investment banking fees of $1,799M, service charges of $1,676M, card income of $1,561M and $352M of other income.

takeaways.text: Net interest income reached $16,449M as loans and deposits grew and old fixed-rate assets repriced to today's higher rates. The net interest yield widened to 2.16%, up 15 basis points from a year ago.
takeaways.title: The lending engine is earning more

takeaways.text: A $1.2B non-deductible regulatory settlement turned a solid quarter into a reported profit decline: net income fell 17% to $6,933M, but excluding the charge it was $8.1B with EPS of $1.08 instead of $0.91.
takeaways.title: One charge explains the profit drop

takeaways.text: The bank returned $8.3B to shareholders ($6.0B of buybacks, $2.2B of dividends) while keeping its CET1 capital ratio at 10.9%. Net charge-offs were $1,349M — 0.44% of loans, slightly better than a year ago.
takeaways.title: Capital is strong and going back to shareholders

verdict: Bank of America's revenue rose 3% to $30.0B with net interest income up 8%, but a one-time $1.2B regulatory settlement cut net income 17% to $6.9B — without it, profit was $8.1B.
